documents: Chalot-Prat, Magott & Berthod (2023), Ocean expansion: The role of detachment faults, Terra Nova 35, 15-22 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: their connections with the distribution of volcanoes on the sea floor are poorly known

sequences.source_document: Chalot-Prat et al. 2023, Terra Nova 35:15-22 (published PDF)

steps.action: The authors state that the relation of slow-ridge detachment faults to volcano distribution, and the stress field that induces them, are poorly known.
steps.quote: their connections with the distribution of volcanoes on the sea floor are poorly known

steps.action: The authors adopt their earlier westward-drift framework, in which lithospheric drift causes top-to-down intra-mantle decoupling and a faster-drifting upper layer, as the working theory.
steps.quote: the westward drift of the lithosphere that induces a top to down intra-mantle decoupling

steps.action: The authors set the aim: show that small-scale active tectonics in the uppermost oceanic lithosphere fits plate kinematic reconstructions that integrate mantle petrology and deformation.
steps.quote: fits well with plate kinematic reconstructions that integrate our knowledge of mantle petrology and mantle deformation at the lithospheric scale

steps.action: The authors select the Chenaillet ophiolite (Alps), a fossil slow-spreading ridge fragment, as the example case.
steps.quote: a well-preserved fragment of a fossil slow-spreading oceanic ridge

steps.action: The authors re-present field, geochemical and structural observations from their earlier studies (Chalot-Prat 2005; Magott et al. 2021): conic vents in comb systems above feeder-dykes on mantle cataclasites, shown on a synthetic map.
steps.quote: demonstrating the space and time emplacement of hundreds of conic volcanic vents along high-angle normal faults

steps.action: The authors interpret the rotational high- to low-angle normal faults that feed and transport the volcanoes as on-axis detachment faults that create new surface.
steps.quote: These rotational (high- to low-angle) normal faults are thus on-axis detachment faults leading to surface creation.

steps.action: The authors read the pseudo-symmetry of the comb systems as small-scale mantle spreading on both sides of the plate boundary, and note that small-scale high-angle faults parallel large-scale low-angle faults.
steps.quote: That pseudosymmetry is interpreted as reflecting, at small scale, the mantle spreading effects on both sides of the plate boundary.

steps.action: The authors describe the low-angle detachment faults and their high-angle conjugates crosscutting the mantle basement (strikes, dips, cataclasites, hydrothermal deposits), following Magott et al. 2021.
steps.quote: These low-angle normal faults are roughly N–S (strikes N160°–N175°) with dips below 15° towards E.

steps.action: The authors report fault-slip inversion into four stress tensors with two σ3 trends (N030° dominant, N060°), interpreted as an alternating stress field.
steps.quote: Inversion of fault-slip data reveals two σ3 palaeostress trends at N030°, the dominant one, and at N060°

steps.action: The authors compare the dominant σ3 with the feeder-dyke and low-angle fault directions, find them consistent, and take N030° as the spreading direction.
steps.quote: the dominant N030°E σ3 is consistent with the NNW–SSE direction of volcano feeder dykes

steps.action: The authors report crosscutting relations: low-angle faults intersect the roots of conic volcanic vents, which therefore lie in the hanging walls.
steps.quote: Low-angle faults intersect roots of conic volcanic vents that thus belong to their hanging walls

steps.action: The authors conclude that volcanism stopped as detachments developed at shallower depth off-axis, and that detachments control mantle transfer, eruption and gabbro sill emplacement.
steps.quote: They attest to active tectonics during oceanic expansion.

steps.action: The authors note that paleomagnetic evidence of footwall rotations at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (Garcés & Gee 2007) supports a model close to theirs.
steps.quote: Their tectonic model of oceanic expansion is close to ours.

steps.action: The authors build a three-step framework (Figure 3), modified from Chalot-Prat et al. 2017, that integrates deep and shallow lithospheric processes under westward drift.
steps.quote: The challenge is now to integrate in a single framework (Figure 3) deep and shallow processes

steps.action: The authors take westward-drift kinematics from the literature (both plates move west at VA > VB; ridge velocity and half-spreading rate) to derive the framework's expectations.
steps.quote: both oceanic plates move to the west

steps.action: The authors take lithosphere thickness and MORB melt-segregation depths from published geophysical and HP-HT experimental work.
steps.quote: MORB (Mid-Oceanic Ridge Basalts) parental melts segregate from residual peridotite between 55 and 45 km depth

steps.action: From the near-primitive, aphyric MORB compositions, the authors propose fast magma ascent along a wide, fractured vertical plate-boundary zone.
steps.quote: This suggests that magma travels along the boundary between the two plates

steps.action: The authors derive, from their earlier model, asymmetric accretion of mantle residues and gabbro trapping on either side of the migrating ridge.
steps.quote: accretion of successive mantle residues at the base of the lithospheric mantle is not symmetric on either side of the plate boundary

steps.action: The authors check the framework against published results: geophysical plate asymmetry (Panza et al. 2010), secondary harzburgites, the Poliakov & Buck explanation of gabbro sills, and cataclasite shear (Mallows & Searle 2012).
steps.quote: resulting in a first-order asymmetry in composition between the two plates, which is confirmed by geophysical data

steps.action: The authors conclude that detachment faults exclusively control surface creation and ocean widening, with drift-driven tectonic stresses directing mantle and magma transfer.
steps.quote: Surface creation leading to ocean widening is exclusively controlled by detachment faults

tree.answer: Detachment faulting and its relation to on-axis volcano feeder-dykes at slow-spreading ridges
No; read from traces in a fossil ophiolite (Chenaillet)
Show that small-scale tectonics fits the westward-drift plate kinematic model
Magmatism as the cause of widening (Morgan 1972) is named as the assumed view but not developed as a tested rival
No distinct predictions derived for the rivals
Conditions found: a fossil slow-spreading ridge preserved as an ophiolite
No variation performed; only consistency with cited literature
Kept: detachment faults control surface creation, framed in the westward-drift model
Two anonymous reviewers acknowledged; no review file supplied

end.claim: Surface creation leading to ocean widening is exclusively controlled by detachment faults, shallow tracers of tectonic stresses induced by the westward drift of the lithosphere, along which mantle and gabbro are transferred and on-axis volcanoes are uprooted.

decisive_move.sentence: The reinterpretation of the Chenaillet rotational high- to low-angle normal faults, which feed and carry the comb volcanoes, as on-axis detachment faults creating new surface is what links volcanism to detachment faulting.

gates.evidence: No new data were acquired; the field, structural and stress data come from Chalot-Prat 2005 and Magott et al. 2021. The claim is assembled by interpretation and by consistency with cited literature, and is not exposed to a test it could fail. Nothing was fixed in advance; the westward-drift model is adopted as the 'working base' (p. 18).

novelty_claims.quote: This is an innovative hypothesis and of broad general interest point of our paper.
[...] finally clarifies the structural relationships between the feeder-dykes of volcanoes on-axis and the low-angle detachment faults
while emphasizing the tectonic point of view, an area so often completely ignored until now

limits: This is a summary and synthesis paper. All primary observations (the map, fault-slip data, stress inversions, vent chronology) come from the authors' earlier work, Chalot-Prat 2005 and Magott et al. 2021, coded as inherited. Lithosphere thickness, melt depths and plate kinematics are cited. No V step is performed here: no replication, robustness test or control. The only checks are cited consistencies (Garcés & Gee 2007; Panza et al. 2010), so the paper's own V is none. The stated rival view (magmatism as the cause of widening, after Morgan 1972) is asserted to be wrong but not tested, which is why the composition is none_fits: it is neither trace_series with stated rivals nor strong_inference. The word 'exclusively' in the headline claim is not supported by any exclusion step. Sub-claims: the three-step deep-to-shallow model (Figure 3) is a conceptual synthesis modified from Chalot-Prat et al. 2017 (status none or best_explanation at most). The alternating N030/N060 stress field is an inherited estimate without stated uncertainty. The plate-boundary magma-pathway width ('several kilometres') is an unquantified inference. Two anonymous reviewers are thanked, and the received and revised dates (6 July, 15 September 2022) imply a revision; no review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded (inference). The paper does not report how the Chenaillet case was chosen over other ophiolites, or any search for counterexamples.

disagreements.target: Morgan (1972) and the view usually assumed since
disagreements.support: Field relations at Chenaillet, from the authors' earlier studies, of feeder-dykes along rotational detachment faults; no test against the rival is performed.
disagreements.quote: magmatism is synchronous with and not the cause of ocean widening, unlike what has usually been assumed since publication of the Morgan paper

disagreements.target: Community neglect of the tectonic view of seafloor spreading
disagreements.support: A multidisciplinary synthesis of small- and large-scale features emphasizing detachment tectonics.
disagreements.quote: while emphasizing the tectonic point of view, an area so often completely ignored until now

disagreements.target: Expectation that ridge-floor mantle rocks are primary harzburgite melting residues
disagreements.support: Cites Piccardo et al. 2007 and Chalot-Prat et al. 2013 showing secondary harzburgite and lherzolite from percolation-reaction.
disagreements.quote: mantle rocks sampled on the floor of the ocean ridge have never a primary harzburgite composition, that is the expected one

alternatives_considered.chosen: N030° σ3 as the spreading direction
alternatives_considered.alternatives: N060° σ3 trend (assigned to dome-structure formation)
alternatives_considered.reason: Dominant trend, consistent with feeder-dyke and low-angle fault directions
